threat_event: Phishing steals the owner's email credentials and relays the SMS code; the attacker reads client correspondence, Client A BCSI copies, and the Client B gateway user name
threat_source: Cybercriminal or nation-state group targeting utility suppliers
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: SMS-based MFA; BCSI copies and gateway details kept in email and files; no phishing training; no sign-in review
regulatory_driver: N22-R01 (CIP-011-3 R1 Part 1.2 via SSA-A (1); SSA-A (8)); CEII NDA (18 CFR 388.113(h)(2))
existing_controls: SMS codes on email; Client A portal MFA
treatment_plan: Authenticator app or security key on email; password manager; delete BCSI copies from email (portal only); monthly sign-in review; annual phishing training

threat_event: Malware picked up while browsing or reading email on the multi-purpose laptop is carried into a Client B relay or substation network during a commissioning visit
threat_source: Cybercriminal group (malware); targeted attacker using the consultant as a path
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: One laptop for email, web, and relay connections; daily administrator account; settings software updated by hand
affected_asset_or_process: SYS-02 laptop; Client B low impact relays; BP-01
regulatory_driver: N22-R01 (CIP-003-9 R2 Att. 1 Sec. 5.2 via VAA-B (1))
existing_controls: Built-in antivirus; automatic OS updates; Client B pre-connection checklist
treatment_plan: Standard daily account now; dedicated field laptop used only for client relay work, with no email or browsing; update settings software before each visit

threat_event: Attacker with the owner's stolen gateway password triggers MFA pushes until one is approved and opens a session into Client B's OT network
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Gateway password saved in the browser; push approvals with no number matching; no written rule to reject unexpected pushes
affected_asset_or_process: SYS-06 Client B gateway account; Client B OT network
regulatory_driver: N22-R01 (CIP-003-9 R2 Att. 1 Sec. 6 via VAA-B (3) and (4))
existing_controls: Client B enables sessions on request only and monitors them
treatment_plan: Password manager only; never approve a push the owner did not start and report it to Client B at once (P08); ask Client B for number matching

threat_event: Client A BCSI reaches a person Client A never authorized (the drafter's shared folder; an open share link); Client A ends the contract or must address its own CIP-004-7 R6 compliance
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: No access agreement with the drafter; shares never reviewed; client folders mixed in one "Projects" folder
affected_asset_or_process: Client A BCSI in SYS-01; BP-03
regulatory_driver: N22-R01 (CIP-004-7 R6 Part 6.1 via SSA-A (2); CIP-011-3 R1 Part 1.2 via SSA-A (1))
existing_controls: Share removed 2026-07-21; Client A notified 2026-07-22; drafter deletion statement 2026-07-29
treatment_plan: Owner-only client folders; external sharing off by default; quarterly share review; signed drafter access agreement; ask Client A before any helper sees its files

threat_event: Photos of client control houses and relay panels sync from the phone to a personal photo cloud with no MFA and are exposed
threat_source: Owner error; account takeover of the photo cloud
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Camera roll sync on; no rule on site photos
treatment_plan: Turn off photo sync; move needed photos to the Client A portal or owner-only client folder; delete cloud copies; site photos only with client permission

threat_event: Laptop or phone is stolen from the vehicle during a site visit
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Devices travel to substations; left in the vehicle during site work
existing_controls: Full-disk encryption; phone encryption; device lock
treatment_plan: Accepted: residual risk Low because both devices are encrypted. Keep devices locked out of sight; report a loss to clients under POL-01 10.2

threat_event: A mixed-use USB drive carries malware from a home or Client C computer to a client relay or engineering workstation
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Same drives for personal and client files; scanned only at Client B
regulatory_driver: N22-R01 (CIP-003-9 R2 Att. 1 Sec. 5.3 via VAA-B (2))
treatment_plan: Two dedicated, labeled drives for settings files, scanned before every site use; personal drives never used for client work

threat_event: Attacker takes over the accounting SaaS and changes the bank details on invoices, so client payments go to the attacker
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: No MFA on the accounting account; password reused
regulatory_driver: Business need (P01); Fla. Stat. 501.171(2) (stored bank and W-9 data)
existing_controls: Clients pay by bank transfer to a known account
treatment_plan: Turn on MFA; unique password; tell clients in writing that bank details never change by email alone

threat_event: Client C load data sent to an AI forecasting SaaS without consent; the provider keeps or trains on it; an unvalidated forecast reaches a sealed planning study
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Trial started before any terms review or client consent; no validation method
affected_asset_or_process: SYS-08 AI tools; Client C data; BP-04
regulatory_driver: Client C contract (confidentiality clause); N22-R01 (CIP-011-3 R1 Part 1.2 via SSA-A (1), chatbot)
treatment_plan: Ask Client C for written consent or rebuild the forecast without the tool; deletion request to the provider; P10 rules for any AI use

threat_event: Owner-engineer is suddenly unavailable or loses the only phone, so nobody can answer clients, send incident notices, or finish field work
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: One person holds every role, credential, and client authorization; no standby engineer
treatment_plan: Standby engineer arrangement with NDA (Client A pre-authorization requested); sealed recovery codes and emergency sheet with the owner's attorney; second client contact

threat_event: Laptop failure or ransomware destroys local settings databases and license files that have no backup
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Local settings databases and license files not backed up; no restore test
existing_controls: File suite version history for files stored there
treatment_plan: Daily encrypted backup of local settings databases and license files to the business suite; quarterly restore test

threat_event: Client BCSI and CEII kept after projects end are exposed later, or a client or FERC asks for proof of return or destruction that cannot be given
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: No client information register; two Client A projects from 2025 never certified
affected_asset_or_process: Client A BCSI; CEII; SYS-01; SYS-02
existing_controls: CEII kept in an encrypted archive
treatment_plan: Client information register; certify the two 2025 Client A projects; return or destroy within 30 days of each project end

threat_event: A cyber incident is not recognized, or the 24-hour client notice is missed, so a client cannot meet its own CIP reporting duties
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: No incident procedure, contact sheet, or training; notices given ad hoc
regulatory_driver: N22-R01 (CIP-013-2 R1 Parts 1.2.1 and 1.2.2 via SSA-A (5); VAA-B (5)); CEII NDA (18 CFR 388.113(h)(2))
existing_controls: 2026-07-22 notice to Client A made within 24 hours
treatment_plan: Adopt the P08 runbook and notification matrix; printed client contact sheet; walkthrough with the IT technician

threat_event: A household device or a nearby attacker on the shared home Wi-Fi attacks the laptop or the router
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Household devices on the business network; default router admin password
existing_controls: Laptop host firewall; SaaS and gateway traffic encrypted
treatment_plan: Separate business network; new router admin password; firmware updates; phone hotspot for gateway sessions until then

threat_event: Hurricane or long power outage closes the home office for several days
existing_controls: All business data in SaaS; laptop can work from anywhere with a hotspot
treatment_plan: Accepted: residual risk Low. Take the laptop, phone, and dedicated USB drives when a storm watch is issued; tell clients of any delay
